type.description: A 'kit' (the Homestead, phase 3, TECH_DESIGN §30) is a building bought as a plan at the workbench's 'Build' tab: its stats name the 'building' (data/buildings) it sets down, in build mode only, as a site that stands the next morning. It never stacks (one of each building), never goes in a chest and is never on the item bar; the build bar shows it. A 'placeable' is set down on the hero's land in build mode, never from the item bar (the Homestead, TECH_DESIGN §30): its stats say whether it lies or stands, and it must stack and name an icon, which is its picture on the ground too (a frame of gameplay/art/placed.png, PlacedArt.FRAMES). A 'sprinkler' is set on tilled, empty soil of the plot from the item button, as a seed is planted, and taken up again with interact; each morning it waters the four cells beside it. A 'material' (stone, wood, ore, coal, a bar, a crystal) is neither eaten nor given, only carried, sold and made into things. 'food' is eaten from the item menu (its stats say what it gives); an 'ingredient' is only cooked with; a 'tool' works the farm from the item button (its stats name which tool it is); a 'seed' is planted from the item button (its stats name its crop).

icon.description: The item's picture (a frame of gameplay/art/items.png, ItemIcons.FRAMES; for a placeable, a frame of gameplay/art/placed.png, PlacedArt.FRAMES). Without one, its type decides.

stats.description: What the item does, by its type. A placeable's: 'layer', and for a standing one 'blocks', 'joins', 'light' and 'grows'. Weapon stats: damage is in enemy health points; ranged weapons name their ammo item id and arrow speed (px/s); bombs have a fuse (s) and blast radius (px); a lantern's radius is how far its light reaches (px).

energy.description: Food: the energy it gives when eaten.

hearts.description: Food: the hearts it mends when eaten (0.5 is half a heart).

crop.description: A seed: the id of the crop it plants (data/crops).

fewer_blows.description: A pickaxe: how many blows fewer than the plain one it needs to break a rock (never less than one blow). The copper pickaxe says 1, the iron one 2.

reach.description: A hoe or a watering can: how many cells in a line one use works, from the cell the hero faces onward. The copper ones say 2, the iron ones 3. The cell he faces decides whether the stroke is made; energy and the pour are paid once.

layer.description: A placeable: 'lying' (a path, a floor, a flower bed: flat, walked over, never in the way) or 'standing' (a fence, a gate, a hedge, a lamp post, a bench, a sapling). A cell of the land holds one of each at most.

fills.description: A lying placeable: its picture covers its cell edge to edge (a path, a floor), so it is drawn with a rim where none lies beside it. A flower bed, which has its own edge, leaves it out.

blocks.description: A standing placeable: whether it fills its cell. A gate says false: the hero walks through it, and it still counts as fence.

joins.description: A standing placeable: it runs on to its neighbours that join too (a fence's rails; its frames '<icon>_e', '<icon>_n' and '<icon>_s' are the rails, and a '<icon>_v' is how it stands in a run going north and south).

light.description: A standing placeable: it shines from dusk to dawn, steadily (a lamp post). Its frame '<icon>_lit' shows it burning.

at.description: Where the light is in its cell, in pixels: [x, y].

grows.description: A standing placeable: a sapling. It needs no water. It shows three pictures as it grows ('<icon>', '<icon>_1', '<icon>_2'), and after 'mornings' it is a tree of kind 'tree', a tall picture the hero walks behind. Taken up, a tree gives back its sapling.

building.description: A kit: the id of the building it sets down (data/buildings). Each building has one kit.

tool.description: 'pick' is the pickaxe, which strikes the rock the hero faces (data/rules/mine.json says how many blows each kind takes). A tool: 'hoe' tills bare soil; 'water' is the watering can, which waters tilled soil and names what it holds as its 'ammo' (that item's max_stack is how many pours it holds). 'cooldown' is how long one use takes (s).
